sentences: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development.
But only if you act him out.
translations: 来自斯特拉特福德的文法学校男孩在开创性研究显示莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展后，取得了学术上的重大突破。
但前提是你得把他表演出来。

sentences: A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.

"The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
translations: 一项研究发现，采用“排练室”方法教授莎士比亚拓宽了儿童的词汇量、写作的复杂性以及他们的情感素养。
“研究表明，演员的工作方式对儿童使用语言的方式以及他们如何看待自己产生了很大影响，”委托进行这项研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）的杰奎·奥汉隆说道。

sentences: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils—aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy".
They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in The Tempest.
The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length.

They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion".

The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
translations: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所州立小学的数百名五年级学生（年龄九至十岁），这些学校此前“未接触过RSC教学法”。
他们被分为目标组和对照组，并被要求例如以《暴风雨》中沉船后的费迪南德的身份写一封瓶中信。
目标组获得了一个30分钟的基于戏剧的活动来配合这段文章。
经过同行评审的结果显示，目标组的学生运用了更广泛的词汇，使用了“被归类为更复杂或更罕见的”词语，并且写作篇幅更长。
他们还“在角色写作中显得更加自如……而[对照组]学生想象自己遭遇海难时的反应，[目标组]儿童则设身处地地扮演文学角色并表达该角色的情感”。
《行动时刻》研究还发现，虽然对照组学生依赖“荒岛陈词滥调”，如棕榈树，但目标组学生“更具扩展性，描绘出天空、海洋和大气状况的更广阔图景”。

sentences: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful".
She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through.
They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes."
The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
translations: 奥汉隆表示，她对“[目标组]儿童写作中明显体现出的情感素养”以及他们“在写作中更具韧性、更充满希望”感到最为惊讶。
她补充道：“情感理解非常明显，这可能与[排练室过程]有关，在这个过程中你习惯于尝试设身处地地想象。”
“他们能够自如地描述不同的情感状态，而戏剧中的一部分就是让你设身处地。”
她说，这项研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

sentences: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist?

O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
translations: 但这些结果能否在任何其他古典剧作家身上复制呢？
奥汉隆表示还需要更多研究，但她指出，莎士比亚使用了20,000个词汇，而日常用语只有2,000个，这为“儿童的生活带来了语言的大规模扩展”，并且这与儿童“运用全身让文字活起来”相结合。

sentences:
21. The "rehearsal room" approach requires pupils to
A. rewrite the lines from Shakespeare
B. watch RSC actors' performances
C. play the roles in Shakespeare
D. study drama under RSC artists
translations:
21. “排练室”方法要求学生
A. 改写莎士比亚的台词
B. 观看RSC演员的表演
C. 扮演莎士比亚戏剧中的角色
D. 在RSC艺术家的指导下学习戏剧

sentences:
22. The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether
A. the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes
B. expanding vocabulary helps develop reading fluency
C. emotion affects understanding of sophisticated works
D. the classroom activity stimulates interest in the arts
translations:
22. 研究将学生分成两组，以探究是否
A. 教学方式的改变能提升学习效果
B. 扩大词汇量有助于培养阅读流畅性
C. 情感影响对复杂作品的理解
D. 课堂活动能激发对艺术的兴趣

sentences:
23. Control pupils' reliance on "desert island clichés" shows their
A. weakness in description
B. omission of small details
C. casual style of writing
D. preference for big words
translations:
23. 对照组学生对“荒岛陈词滥调”的依赖显示出他们的
A. 描述能力薄弱
B. 忽视细节
C. 随意的写作风格
D. 偏爱大词

sentences:
24. What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon?
A. Writing in an imaginative manner.
B. Identifying with literary characters.
C. Drawing inspiration from nature.
D. Concentrating on real-life situations.
translations:
24. 根据奥汉隆的说法，什么能促进儿童的情感素养？
A. 以富有想象力的方式写作。
B. 与文学角色产生共鸣。
C. 从自然中汲取灵感。
D. 专注于现实生活情境。

sentences:
25. It can be inferred from the last paragraph that
A. the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare
B. the language of Shakespeare may be formidable for pupils
C. other old dramatists may be included in primary education
D. pupils may be reluctant to work on other old dramatists
translations:
25. 从最后一段可以推断出
A. 新的教学方法可能最适合莎士比亚作品
B. 莎士比亚的语言可能对学生来说难以掌握
C. 其他古典剧作家可能被纳入初等教育
D. 学生可能不愿意学习其他古典剧作家的作品
